mainTopic: Whether a person who lives in someone else's courtyard without permission must pay: the case of זה נהנה וזה לא חסר (one person benefits and the other loses nothing)
overview: רב חסדא asks about someone who lives in another person's courtyard without permission, where the owner was not going to rent it out anyway. The squatter benefits, but the owner loses nothing. This case is called זה נהנה וזה לא חסר. רמי בר חמא tries to prove from a משנה about an animal eating produce that the one who benefits must pay, but רבא says that case is not the same. The גמרא then tries proofs from several other sources: the משנה about fencing a field surrounded on all sides, and the משנה about a collapsed house and its upper story. Each proof is pushed away, because the case turns out to be special or to involve some loss after all. The question is sent to רבי אמי, who rules the squatter is פטור, while רבי חייא בר אבא admits he has no answer. Two students then give opposite reports of רבי יוחנן's view. רב פפא explains that רבי אבהו's report, that the squatter pays, came from an inference about a הקדש treasurer, together with רבי יוחנן's silence, which was not agreement. The גמרא begins explaining, with a rule of רבה, why הקדש is different, and this explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The owner's argument: you benefited
steps.stepSummary: The question ends with the courtyard owner's claim that the squatter benefited and should pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you benefited!
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining רב חסדא's question in the middle. This last line gives the owner's side: 'You got something out of my property, so pay me.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The squatter's side is that the owner lost nothing, since the courtyard was not for rent. The owner's side is that the squatter still saved money he would have spent elsewhere. The question is which side wins: does a benefit with no loss create a duty to pay?

keyTerms.meaning: You benefited / you got enjoyment from it
One person benefits and the other loses nothing

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new question. It is the last half of רב חסדא's question, which began just before this section.

phrases.english: But you benefited!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב חסדא's question, which started before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does someone who benefited, while the other side lost nothing, have to pay?

steps.title: רמי בר חמא says a משנה already answers it
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא answers that this question is already settled by a משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is a משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא tells רב חסדא that he does not need to wonder about this, because a משנה already gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He has not yet said which משנה or what it rules. He is only claiming that there is an existing source. That sets up the next question: which משנה?

keyTerms.meaning: It is (already in) a משנה

phrases.english: He said to him: It is a Mishnah.
phrases.notes: רמי בר חמא is talking to רב חסדא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by pointing to an existing משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer can be found in a משנה.

steps.title: Which משנה, and a small act of service first
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks which משנה. רמי בר חמא asks him to serve him first, and רב חסדא folds his scarf.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which משנה? He said to him: After you serve me. He took his scarf and folded it for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא asks which משנה is meant. Before answering, רמי בר חמא asks for a small act of service, and רב חסדא folds his scarf for him. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Serving a teacher was a way of showing respect before receiving Torah from him. רב חסדא accepts the request, so the answer now follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Which משנה?
After you serve me
His scarf

phrases.english: Which Mishnah?
He said to him: When you serve me.
phrases.notes: He means, 'I'll tell you after you do me a small service.'

phrases.english: He took his scarf and folded it for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the specific source behind the claim in step 2.

steps.title: The משנה: an animal pays for what it benefited
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא quotes the משנה. If an animal benefits from eating produce in the public domain, its owner pays for the benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it benefited, it pays what it benefited.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא now gives the source. It is the משנה about an animal that ate produce in the public domain. The owner pays for whatever the animal benefited.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an animal eating in the public domain does not make its owner pay for the damage. Even so, the משנה makes him pay for the benefit. רמי בר חמא learns from this that benefit alone creates a duty to pay, so the squatter must pay too.

keyTerms.meaning: It (the animal) benefited
It pays (meaning, its owner pays)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main proof offered for the squatter case. The rest of the section tests whether it really fits.

phrases.english: He said to him: If it benefited,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה from earlier in this פרק about an animal eating produce in the public domain.

phrases.english: it pays what it benefited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the specific משנה that was asked for in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: Someone who benefits must pay, so the squatter must pay.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: an animal that benefited in the public domain pays what it benefited.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה does not really match
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רב חסדא accepted the proof only because Heaven helped רמי בר חמא. In truth the משנה is a case where one side lost, and the courtyard is a case where nobody lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How little does a man whose Master helps him need to worry. Even though it does not match the משנה, he accepted it from him. This (the משנה) is 'one benefits and the other loses,' and that (the courtyard) is 'one benefits and the other does not lose'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא points out that the proof does not really fit. He says רב חסדא accepted it anyway, as if Heaven was on רמי בר חמא's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the produce owner lost his food, so it is זה נהנה וזה חסר. In the courtyard case, the owner lost nothing, so it is זה נהנה וזה לא חסר. Paying when there was a real loss tells us nothing about paying when there was no loss.

keyTerms.meaning: His Master (Heaven) helps him
It is not similar / does not match
One benefits and the other loses

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is a case of benefit plus loss. The courtyard is a case of benefit with no loss. So, according to רבא, the משנה does not prove the courtyard case.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: כַּמָּה לָא חָלֵי וְלָא מַרְגֵּישׁ
phrases.english: Rava said: How much does he not get sick and not feel (worried)
phrases.notes: Literally 'not sick and not feeling,' meaning he has nothing to worry about.

phrases.english: a man whose Master helps him.
phrases.notes: 'His Master' means ה׳.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא דָּמֵי לְמַתְנִיתִין,
phrases.english: For even though it does not match the Mishnah,
he accepted it from him.
phrases.notes: רב חסדא accepted the proof from רמי בר חמא.

phrases.english: This is 'one benefits and the other loses,'

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי זֶה נֶהֱנֶה וְזֶה לֹא חָסֵר הוּא!
phrases.english: and that is 'one benefits and the other does not lose'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כַּמָּה לָא חָלֵי וְלָא מַרְגֵּישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the משנה brought in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof itself. It does not decide the courtyard question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה involves a loss to the produce owner, but the courtyard case involves no loss.

steps.title: Defending רמי בר חמא: produce in public is ownerless
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רמי בר חמא's view. Produce left in the public domain is treated as given up by its owner, so in the משנה nobody really lost anything either.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רמי בר חמא? Ordinary produce in the public domain, the owner makes it ownerless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רמי בר חמא still thought the משנה fits. He holds that produce left in the public domain is treated as ownerless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner gave up the produce, he lost nothing when the animal ate it. So the משנה is also a case of זה נהנה וזה לא חסר, just like the courtyard. That makes it a fair proof that benefit alone requires payment.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary produce (with nothing said about who owns it)
The public domain
He makes them ownerless (הפקר)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רמי בר חמא, the משנה is also a case of 'no loss,' because produce left in public is הפקר. So the animal's owner pays for benefit alone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defense keeps alive the idea that benefit alone may require payment, which is the question the sugya is trying to settle.

phrases.english: And Rami bar Hama?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking how רמי בר חמא could compare the two cases.

phrases.english: Ordinary produce in the public domain,
he (the owner) makes it ownerless.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָמֵי בַּר חָמָא סְתַם פֵּירוֹת בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's rejection by explaining the case in the משנה differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the case in the משנה differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא assumed the produce owner in the משנה suffered a loss.
steps.terutzMaskana: Produce left in public is ownerless, so there was no loss, and the משנה matches the courtyard case.

steps.title: A proof from the surrounded field: the neighbor must pay
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. If someone's fields surround his neighbor's field and he fences all four sides, the neighbor must share the cost. It looks like proof that in זה נהנה וזה לא חסר, the one who benefits is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: if a person's fields surround his friend's field on three sides, and he fenced the first, second and third sides, the court does not make the friend pay. That means if he fenced the fourth side too, the court does make him pay. Learn from this: when one person benefits and the other loses nothing, the one who benefits must pay!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof from a משנה to answer the open question of זה נהנה וזה לא חסר. It reads the משנה closely to suggest that the one who benefits must pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only three sides fenced, the inner field is still open, so its owner gets no real benefit and pays nothing. The גמרא reads this to mean that once all four sides are fenced, the inner owner must pay. The outer owner needed fences for his own fields anyway, so he seems to lose nothing, and the inner owner still pays. That looks like a ruling of חייב in זה נהנה וזה לא חסר.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
The one who surrounds; the owner of the outer fields
Sides (literally 'directions')
He built a fence
Learn from this; a formula for drawing a conclusion

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה itself only speaks about three sides. The ruling for the fourth side comes from the גמרא's inference ('הָא רְבִיעִית'), not from the words of the משנה.

phrases.english: We learned: one whose fields surround his fellow's field
phrases.notes: This משנה is in בבא בתרא.

phrases.english: on three of its sides,

phrases.aramaic: וְגָדַר אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה וְאֶת הַשְּׁנִיָּה וְאֶת הַשְּׁלִישִׁית –
phrases.english: and he fenced the first, the second, and the third sides
the court does not obligate him (the inner owner) to pay.
This implies that if the fourth side was fenced, the court does obligate him;
Learn from this:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה נֶהֱנֶה וְזֶה לֹא חָסֵר – חַיָּיב!
phrases.english: when this one benefits and that one loses nothing, he is obligated to pay!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the produce משנה was weakened in steps 5-6, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That in זה נהנה וזה לא חסר the one who benefits is חייב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of הַמַּקִּיף, read by inference: if the fourth side is fenced, the inner owner must pay.

steps.title: Rejected: the inner field made the fence longer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Here the outer owner did lose something, because the inner field forced him to build a longer fence.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the outer owner can say to him: 'You caused me to build a longer fence around everything.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 7. It shows that the fence case is not truly a case where the other side lost nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the inner field in the way, the מקיף could have fenced his own land along a shorter line. Because the inner field sits there, his fence runs longer and costs more. So this is really זה נהנה וזה חסר, and paying there tells us nothing about our question.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; used to push away a proof
You caused
An extra-long fence around the land

phrases.english: It is different there,
because he (the outer owner) can say to him:
You caused me an extra-long fence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects the proof of step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof is rejected because the case does not fit, not because the reasoning was wrong.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The outer owner did lose money (a longer fence), so the case is זה נהנה וזה חסר.

steps.title: A proof from רבי יוסי: the neighbor is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי from the same משנה. The inner owner pays everything only if he built the fourth fence himself. By inference, if the outer owner built it, the inner owner is exempt. That looks like proof for פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יוסי said, if the surrounded owner got up and fenced the fourth side, the court makes him pay his share of everything. The reason is that the surrounded owner built it. But if the surrounding owner built it, the inner owner is exempt. Learn from this: when one person benefits and the other loses nothing, he is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another proof from the next part of the same משנה. This time the proof points the other way, toward פטור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי makes the inner owner pay only when he himself built the fourth fence, which shows he wanted it. The גמרא infers that if the מקיף built the fourth fence, the ניקף pays nothing even though he benefits. That looks like a ruling of פטור in זה נהנה וזה לא חסר.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; introduces a source brought as proof
The one who is surrounded; the owner of the inner field
They roll onto him; the court makes him pay his share
The reason; used to infer what happens in the opposite case
Exempt; does not have to pay

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two proofs. Step 7 tried to prove the one who benefits must pay (חייב). This step tries to prove the opposite (פטור), from the same משנה.

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Yosei said:
If the surrounded owner got up
and fenced the fourth side
the court makes him pay his share of all of it.
phrases.notes: 'All of it' means all four fences, not just the one he built.

phrases.english: The reason is that the surrounded owner built the fence,
which implies that if the surrounding owner built it, the inner owner is exempt;
Learn from this,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה נֶהֱנֶה וְזֶה לֹא חָסֵר – פָּטוּר!
phrases.english: when this one benefits and that one loses nothing, he is exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof for חייב was rejected, the גמרא tries the rest of the same משנה, which seems to point to פטור.
steps.raayaObject: That in זה נהנה וזה לא חסר the one who benefits is פטור
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי in the משנה of הַמַּקִּיף, read by inference: if the מקיף built the fourth fence, the ניקף is exempt.

steps.title: Rejected: the inner owner only needed cheap protection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this proof too. The inner owner can say he would have been happy with cheap protection worth one זוז, so he does not have to pay for an expensive fence.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the inner owner can say to him: 'For me, protection worth one זוז would have been enough.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 9, so the question of זה נהנה וזה לא חסר stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ניקף is exempt not because a person who benefits never pays. He is exempt because he never needed such an expensive fence. A cheap form of protection would have been enough for him, so he does not have to pay for the big fence. When he builds the fourth fence himself, he shows he does want the full fence, so then he pays.

keyTerms.meaning: For me
It is enough for me
Protection or guarding
A זוז, a small coin

steps.whatToRemember: Both readings of the fence משנה were pushed away. In the first part the outer owner did lose money (a longer fence). In רבי יוסי's part the inner owner did not really need a costly fence. So this משנה does not settle זה נהנה וזה לא חסר.

phrases.english: It is different there,
because he (the inner owner) can say to him:
For me it would have been enough
to have protection worth one זוז.
phrases.notes: He means a cheap form of protection. Why should I pay for your expensive fence?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects the proof of step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof is rejected because of the special facts of the case, not because of a general rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ניקף never wanted such a costly fence, so the case cannot teach that a person who benefits is always פטור.

steps.title: Proof from the collapsed house and upper story: no rent is owed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. When a house and its upper story collapse and the lower owner refuses to rebuild, the upper owner may rebuild and live below until he is paid back his expenses only. Since no rent is taken off, the one who benefits seems to be פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A house and an upper story belong to two people, and they collapsed. The upper-story owner told the house owner to rebuild, and he refused. The upper-story owner may build the house and live in it until the owner pays back his expenses. Only the expenses are owed, not rent for living there. Learn from this that in זה נהנה וזה לא חסר, the one who benefits is פטור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof from a משנה. It shows a person living in someone else's house for free, and no rent is charged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The upper owner benefits by living in the lower house. The lower owner loses nothing, because he did not want to build or use it anyway. The משנה only makes the lower owner pay back the building costs and never deducts rent, so it looks like the one who benefits is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. This introduces a proof from a source.
A house (the lower floor) and an upper story owned by different people
The owner of the upper story
His expenses, meaning the building costs
His rent, meaning payment for living there
One person benefits and the other loses nothing

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A house and an upper story belonging to two people, which collapsed;

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר בַּעַל הָעֲלִיָּיה לְבַעַל הַבַּיִת לִבְנוֹת,
phrases.english: the upper-story owner told the house owner to build,
and he does not want to –
the upper-story owner may build the house
and live in it,
until he pays him his expenses.
phrases.notes: The house owner can't take his house back until he pays the upper owner for building it.

phrases.aramaic: יְצִיאוֹתָיו הוּא דִּמְחַיֵּיב לֵיהּ בַּעַל הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: It is his expenses that the house owner owes him,
but his rent – no;
phrases.notes: No rent is taken off the bill for the time the upper owner lived downstairs.

phrases.english: learn from it:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה נֶהֱנֶה וְזֶה לֹא חָסֵר – פָּטוּר!
phrases.english: one benefits and the other loses nothing – exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַבַּיִת וְהָעֲלִיָּיה שֶׁל שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the fence proofs in Steps 7-10 are rejected, the גמרא brings a new משנה.
steps.raayaObject: זה נהנה וזה לא חסר – פטור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in בבא מציעא about the collapsed house and upper story. It requires repayment of expenses only, with no rent.

steps.title: Rejection: the lower house owes a home to the upper story
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The lower house is obligated to the upper story, so the upper owner lives there by right and not as a free tenant.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the house is obligated to the upper story.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 11. It says that case is special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lower house is the base the upper story stands on, so it is 'bound' to serve the upper owner. That means the upper owner has a right to use it while the building is down. That is why no rent is owed, and it teaches nothing about ordinary זה נהנה וזה לא חסר.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there. This is a standard way to reject a proof.
The house, meaning the lower floor
Is obligated or bound to serve

phrases.english: It is different there,
because the house is bound to the upper story.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide the question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The upper owner has a legal right to the lower house, so this is not a case of benefiting from someone else's property for free.

steps.title: Proof from רבי יהודה: even a squatter pays rent
steps.stepSummary: In the same משנה, רבי יהודה says that even someone who lives in another's courtyard without permission must pay rent. That seems to prove that in זה נהנה וזה לא חסר, the one who benefits is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says: Even one who lives in his friend's courtyard without his knowledge must pay him rent. Learn from this that in זה נהנה וזה לא חסר, the one who benefits is חייב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof for the other side, from רבי יהודה in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first view and says the upper owner must pay rent. He compares it to anyone who lives in someone else's courtyard without asking. Since a squatter pays even when the owner seems to lose nothing, this looks like proof that the one who benefits is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: One who lives in his friend's courtyard
Without his knowledge or permission
To pay him rent
Obligated to pay

phrases.english: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says:
even this one who lives in his friend's courtyard
without his knowledge –
must pay him rent.
Learn from it:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה נֶהֱנֶה וְזֶה לֹא חָסֵר – חַיָּיב!
phrases.english: one benefits and the other loses nothing – obligated!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 11 tried to prove פטור. Now the גמרא tries to prove חייב from the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: זה נהנה וזה לא חסר – חייב
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's statement in the משנה that a person living in another's courtyard without permission pays rent.

steps.title: Rejection: living there blackens the walls
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Living in a house blackens the walls, so the owner does lose something.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because of the blackening of the walls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from רבי יהודה in Step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone lives in a house, smoke and use make the walls dirty, and the house is worth less. So the owner is losing something, and this is not a case of 'the other loses nothing.' The rent is payment for that loss, which proves nothing about pure זה נהנה וזה לא חסר.

keyTerms.meaning: Blackening or soot
Walls

phrases.english: It is different there,
because of the blackening of the walls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof for חייב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The owner does suffer a loss, because his walls get blackened, so this is really זה נהנה וזה חסר.

steps.title: רבי אמי rules that the squatter owes nothing
steps.stepSummary: The proofs did not settle the question, so it is sent to רבי אמי's study hall. He answers: what did the squatter do to the owner, what did he make him lose, how did he damage him? So he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent the question to רבי אמי's study hall. He said: What did he do to him, what did he make him lose, and how did he damage him?
steps.whatsHappening: Since no proof worked, the question is sent to a great sage. רבי אמי answers that the person who benefited does not have to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי's three questions are a short way of saying 'no harm, no payment.' The owner lost nothing, so the one who benefited owes nothing. This is a clear ruling of פטור in זה נהנה וזה לא חסר.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent it, meaning they sent the question
The study hall of רבי אמי
Caused him a loss
Damaged him

phrases.english: They sent it to the study hall of רבי אמי,
phrases.notes: "It" is the original question: someone living in another's courtyard without permission.

phrases.english: he said: And what did he do to him,
and what loss did he cause him, and how did he damage him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: All the proofs were rejected, so the question goes to an outside authority.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אמי rules פטור: the owner suffered no loss or damage, so no payment is due.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אמי's questions are not asking for information. They are a rhetorical way of saying the squatter did nothing wrong, so he is פטור.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר אבא admits he has no answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא says he will think about it. When they send the question again, he says: if I had found a reason, wouldn't I have sent it to you?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: Let us think about the matter. They sent it to him again. He said: They keep sending me this question! If I had found a reason, would I not have sent it to them?
steps.whatsHappening: The question is also sent to רבי חייא בר אבא. He never gives an answer, and in the end he says openly that he has none.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His first reply, 'let us think,' is really a polite way of saying he is unsure. When they ask again, he explains that his silence itself was the answer: he had found no reason to decide. So from him, the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us think the matter over
Again, or then afterward
I found
A reason or explanation

steps.whatToRemember: No proof from a משנה settled זה נהנה וזה לא חסר. Every proof was rejected because the case was special or involved some loss. רבי אמי rules פטור, while רבי חייא בר אבא admits he has no answer.

phrases.english: רבי חייא בר אבא said:
Let us think over the matter.

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַר שַׁלְּחוּהָ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: They sent it again before רבי חייא בר אבא,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: כּוּלֵּיהּ הַאי שָׁלְחוּ לִי וְאָזְלִי!
phrases.english: he said: They keep on sending me this!
If I had found a reason for it,
would I not have sent it to them?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר: נִתְיַישֵּׁב בַּדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי אמי's answer, the גמרא reports that רבי חייא בר אבא gave no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי חייא בר אבא could not resolve the question. רבי אמי alone gives a clear ruling of פטור.

steps.title: Two opposite reports of רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא reports that רבי יוחנן says the squatter does not have to pay rent. רבי אבהו reports that רבי יוחנן says he must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב כהנא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: He does not need to pay him rent. רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: He needs to pay him rent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source on the squatter question: two students quote their teacher רבי יוחנן, and each one quotes him differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is the one from the earlier steps: someone lives in a courtyard that is not his, and the owner was not going to rent it out anyway. According to רב כהנא, רבי יוחנן says the squatter is פטור. According to רבי אבהו, רבי יוחנן says he is חייב. Now the question is which report is the real one.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was stated": it introduces a statement or argument among the אמוראים.
To pay him rent (literally, "to raise up payment for him").
An אמורא who reports רבי יוחנן's view here.
A student of רבי יוחנן who reports the opposite view.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not רב כהנא and רבי אבהו arguing with each other. Both are reporting what רבי יוחנן said, and their reports do not match.

phrases.aramaic: אִתְּמַר, רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Kahana said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
He does not need to pay him rent.
Rabbi Abbahu said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
He needs to pay him rent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר, רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the replies of רבי אמי (פטור) and רבי חייא בר אבא (no answer) in Steps 15-16, the גמרא brings reports from אמוראים of רבי יוחנן's position on the same question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two conflicting reports of רבי יוחנן's view. רב כהנא says the squatter is פטור, and רבי אבהו says he is חייב.

steps.title: רב פפא: רבי אבהו's version was only inferred
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says רבי יוחנן never said outright that the squatter must pay. רבי אבהו inferred it: he drew a conclusion from a related case in front of רבי יוחנן, and רבי יוחנן stayed silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: That statement of רבי אבהו was not said explicitly. Rather, it was said by inference.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains where רבי אבהו's version comes from. This also sets up the next step, where the גמרא quotes the source he inferred it from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An explicit statement is stronger than a conclusion someone draws on his own. By calling רבי אבהו's version an inference, רב פפא weakens it. If the inference turns out to be shaky, רב כהנא's report (פטור) is left standing.

keyTerms.meaning: Explicitly, said outright.
By inference, worked out from a related statement.
A later אמורא who explains the source of the report.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הָא דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ –
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: That statement of Rabbi Abbahu,
was not stated explicitly,
rather, it was stated by inference.
phrases.notes: He means רבי אבהו worked this out himself. רבי יוחנן never said it; he only stayed silent, as the next steps show.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ לָאו בְּפֵירוּשׁ אִתְּמַר, אֶלָּא מִכְּלָלָא אִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the second of the two reports in Step 17 and questions how strong it is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אבהו's report that רבי יוחנן holds the squatter must pay was an inference, not an explicit statement.

steps.title: The משנה about a treasurer using a הקדש stone
steps.stepSummary: The source of the inference is a משנה in מעילה. If a treasurer takes a הקדש stone or beam, he has not committed מעילה. If he gives it to someone else, he has. If he builds it into his house, he commits מעילה only once he has lived under it for a פרוטה's worth.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If he took a stone or a beam of הקדש, he has not committed מעילה. If he gave it to his friend, he has committed מעילה and his friend has not. If he built it into his house, he has not committed מעילה until he lives under it for a פרוטה's worth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה from which רבי אבהו drew his inference. This step lays out the source; the actual inference comes after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is about the הקדש treasurer, the גזבר. Anything in his hands still counts as belonging to הקדש. So simply taking the stone is not מעילה, but handing it to someone else takes it out of הקדש. Building it into his house is not yet מעילה. It becomes מעילה once he has enjoyed living under it for a פרוטה's worth. This means he is responsible for benefiting from it even though הקדש lost nothing. That looks like being חייב in זה נהנה וזה לא חסר.

keyTerms.meaning: Property dedicated to the בית המקדש.
He committed מעילה, meaning he misused הקדש property for personal benefit.
A wooden beam.
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest amount of value that counts in halacha.
"As we learned" in a משנה.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is where רבי אבהו's version comes from. If benefiting from הקדש without causing any loss is enough for מעילה, then perhaps benefiting from a friend's property without causing him any loss also requires payment.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: נָטַל אֶבֶן אוֹ קוֹרָה שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ –
phrases.english: As we learned: If he took a stone or a beam of consecrated property,
phrases.notes: "He" is the treasurer in charge of הקדש, so just taking it doesn't count yet as removing it from הקדש. It's from מעילה 5:4.

phrases.english: he has not committed misuse.
If he gave it to his friend, he has committed misuse,
and his friend has not committed misuse.

phrases.aramaic: בְּנָאָהּ לְתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ – הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא מָעַל,
phrases.english: If he built it into his house, he has not committed misuse,
until he lives beneath it for the value of a peruta.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: נָטַל אֶבֶן אוֹ קוֹרָה שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind the inference that רב פפא described in Step 18.
steps.raayaObject: The basis for רבי אבהו's report that רבי יוחנן holds a person who benefits must pay, even when the owner loses nothing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מעילה 5:4: a treasurer who builds a הקדש stone into his house commits מעילה once he has lived under it for a פרוטה's worth.

steps.title: שמואל: only when the stone covers a skylight
steps.stepSummary: שמואל limits the משנה. It is talking about a case where the stone was just placed over the opening of a skylight, not built into the walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: This is when he placed it over the opening of a skylight.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל adds an important detail about the case in the משנה. This finishes setting up the case that רבי אבהו will draw his inference from in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the stone were actually built into the structure, the stone itself would be changed, and he would commit מעילה right away. Because it only sits over the skylight and can easily be removed, he does not commit מעילה by putting it there. The only מעילה is the benefit of living under it. So this case is pure benefit with no change to the stone.

keyTerms.meaning: A skylight, an opening in the roof.
Over the opening of.
"And that is when...": a phrase that limits a ruling to a specific situation.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: וְהוּא שֶׁהִנִּיחָהּ עַל פִּי אֲרוּבָּה.
phrases.english: And Shmuel said: And this is when he placed it over the opening of a skylight.
phrases.notes: In other words, the stone was just laid on top and not built into the wall. That is why putting it there was not yet מעילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: וְהוּא שֶׁהִנִּיחָהּ עַל פִּי אֲרוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the case of the משנה in Step 19 so that the only מעילה is the benefit of living under the stone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's case is one where the הקדש stone was placed over a skylight and not built into the structure, so the only מעילה comes from living under it.

steps.title: רבי אבהו draws the squatter ruling from the treasurer case, and רבי יוחנן stays silent
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו, sitting before רבי יוחנן, said in the name of שמואל that the משנה about the treasurer shows a squatter must pay rent. רבי יוחנן did not respond.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו sat before רבי יוחנן and said in שמואל's name: This teaches that someone who lives in another person's courtyard without permission must pay him rent. רבי יוחנן stayed silent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is telling the story of how רבי אבהו came to believe that רבי יוחנן holds a squatter must pay. He made the inference out loud in front of רבי יוחנן, and רבי יוחנן said nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The treasurer in the משנה commits מעילה just by living under the הקדש beam, even though he did not damage it. רבי אבהו, quoting שמואל, reasons that the squatter is the same: he gets a benefit, so he must pay. This is the 'other case' רב פפא mentioned in Step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: "This teaches": a conclusion drawn from a source
Someone who lives in another person's courtyard
Without the owner's knowledge or permission
To pay him rent
And he was silent

steps.whyThisMatters: This is where רבי אבהו's version of רבי יוחנן's opinion (Step 17) comes from. It was never a direct quote.

phrases.aramaic: וְיָתֵיב רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Abbahu sat before Rabbi Yochanan,
and was saying in the name of Shmuel:
This teaches,
phrases.notes: He's drawing a lesson from the משנה about the treasurer who lived under the הקדש beam (Step 19).

phrases.english: one who lives in another's courtyard without his knowledge
must pay him rent;
and he was silent to him.
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יוחנן. He gave no answer at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the משנה from Step 19 was turned into a ruling about squatters, as רב פפא described in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אבהו in the name of שמואל, a squatter must pay rent, based on the treasurer case.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's silence was not agreement
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו thought רבי יוחנן's silence meant he agreed. The גמרא says no: רבי יוחנן simply did not pay attention.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו thought: since he was silent, he agrees. But that is not so. He just did not pay attention to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that רבי יוחנן agreed with רבי אבהו. His silence only meant he was not paying attention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו reported 'רבי יוחנן says the squatter must pay' because רבי יוחנן did not object. The גמרא takes that support away, since silence here proves nothing. That leaves רב כהנא's report, that the squatter does not pay, as רבי יוחנן's real view.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees
But that is not so
He did not pay attention at all

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן never agreed that a squatter must pay. רבי אבהו's report came from his own inference plus a silence he misread.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume silence always means agreement. Here the גמרא says outright that רבי יוחנן was silent only because he was not paying attention.

phrases.english: He thought:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אבהו.

phrases.english: since he was silent, he agrees with him.
But that is not so;
he simply did not pay attention to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion רבי אבהו drew from רבי יוחנן's silence in Step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that רבי יוחנן's silence showed he agreed that a squatter must pay.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The silence came from not paying attention, not from agreement.

steps.title: Beginning to explain why the treasurer is different: רבה's rule about הקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain why the treasurer commits מעילה even though a squatter would not pay, using a rule of רבה about הקדש used without permission.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like רבה's view, as רבה said: Consecrated property used without permission...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It starts quoting רבה to show why the treasurer case is special. The quote continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוחנן holds the squatter does not pay, someone could ask why the treasurer in the משנה is liable. The גמרא answers that הקדש follows its own rule, which רבה states. So the treasurer case cannot be used to teach about an ordinary squatter.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with the view of רבה
Consecrated property used without permission

phrases.english: In accordance with Rabba,
phrases.notes: This explains why the treasurer in the משנה is liable even though a squatter is not.

phrases.english: as Rabba said:
Consecrated property, without knowledge –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבי יוחנן's view is that the squatter does not pay, the גמרא explains why the treasurer case from Step 19 is different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: הקדש follows a special rule that does not apply to ordinary property.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The treasurer's liability for living under the beam shows that any squatter who benefits must pay.
steps.terutzMaskana: The treasurer is liable because of a special rule about הקדש (רבה's statement), so ordinary squatters are not affected.
